title: Privacy Surfaces: Logs, Clipboard, Screenshots, and Errors Check

questions.prompt: Which design best applies privacy surfaces: logs, clipboard, screenshots, and errors?
options: Classify and minimise data before it reaches secondary surfaces, centralise redaction, and test release failure paths.
Log full payloads and rely on access control
Put tokens on the clipboard for debugging
Show backend exception text directly to users
questions.answer: Classify and minimise data before it reaches secondary surfaces, centralise redaction, and test release failure paths.
questions.explanation: The strongest option enforces authority at the correct boundary and includes limitations, lifecycle, adversarial verification, and recovery.

questions.prompt: Hashing a low-entropy identifier always makes it anonymous and safe to log.
questions.explanation: Redacting only the happy path leaves tokens and personal data exposed when generic exception logging serialises failed requests and headers.

questions.prompt: What should a user-facing security error contain?
questions.answer: A safe explanation, a next action, and an opaque support identifier—not secrets or internal policy details.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the specific security property and boundary required by the lesson rather than naming a library.
